newsitem.title: USA: Invacare plans Healthdyne share sales.
newsitem.headline: Invacare plans Healthdyne share sales.

text.p: Invacare Corp blasted a plan by hostile target Healthdyne Technologies Inc to alter its bylaws and said it would sell part or all of its Healthdyne shares even while pursuing a proxy fight.

"They have had a full month after announcing their intention to 'explore alternatives'...to negotiate and announce a sale transaction. If they were serious about selling the company, they would have announced a deal by now," Invacare Chief Executive Officer Malachi Mixon said in a news release.

Earlier Wednesday, Healthdyne said an unnamed buyer is willing to pay more for the medical device firm than the $200 million offered by hostile bidder Invacare Corp. It also announced plans to change the threshold needed by shareholders to call a special meeting and amend its poison pill.
Invacare denounced the Healthdyne announcements, saying the incumbent board "continues to try to get re-elected on nothing but rhetoric and empty promises."
It also called the change in the special meeting threshold "a ploy," saying Healthdyne would still be able to schedule a special meeting four months after getting a request.

In announcing its intent to sell at least part of its Healthdyne stake, Invacare cited "rampant speculation in the market." Shares of Healthdyne have been trading above Invacare's $15 per share offer on speculation that a transaction will take place at a higher price.

"Therefore, although we had originally been prepared to await the results of the (July 30 annual) meeting, we now intend beginning as early as tomorrow, based on market conditions, to protect our investment by selling some or all of our Healthdyne shares through market and/or private transactions," Invacare said.
Healthdyne had set a shareholder record date of June 23 for its annual meeting. Invacare said it is the record holder of 600,000 shares for the meeting.

Invacare, which is seeking to install a slate of four directors to take control of Healthdyne's seven-member board, also said it did not object to any of the current directors continuing to serve in the minority.
